keywords: Wellbeing 2.Character strengths 3.Interpersonal communication 4.Best possible self 5.Goals and pathways
educationalGoal: In this course, students will look at their own life from a positive perspective in order to find meaningful purpose. There will be many positive psychology exercises which include building interpersonal communication skills. Students are expected to actively participate in the exercises. Activities are intended to help students become aware of their psychological wellbeing, find meaning in life, and learn more about their place in this diverse world.
advice: Students will receive either a “pass” or “fail” grade for this course. There will be many psychological exercises and group activities in the course. Students will utilize their non-cognitive skills such as empathy and compassion more than their cognitive skills which are usually required for academic courses. Students will be asked to actively participate in experiential learning activities such as psychological exercises and group work (workshops). Students will complete homework activities and discuss the content during in-class activities.
requiredKnowledge: Ability to observe things objectively - (e.g., Not only find negative, but also positive things in your life.) Perseverance - (e.g., Attending every class.) Diligence - (e.g., Complete homework according to the given instructions.) Ability to plan appropriately - (e.g., 1) Conduct group work with an awareness of the time. 2) Be aware of deadlines in order to complete homework on time.) Positive attitude - (e.g., Actively participate in the positive psychology activities.)

activityGoals.body: Realize and appreciate your own character strengths.
Notice and appreciate the positive things in your daily life.
Listen to others actively and constructively.
When necessary, be assertive in expressing your opinions to others.
Thoughtfully consider the pathways to your ideal future self.

achievementLevels.ideal: You can identify and appreciate your character strengths, and you are beginning to utilize them. You can find positive events in your daily life easily. You are prepared to live your life positively even in the face of difficulties. You can imagine your ideal self in 5 years and consider several realistic pathways to reach your ideal future self. You have already begun to practice some of them. You have several coping strategies to use for when your plans in life don’t go according to your intention.
achievementLevels.standard: You can identify and appreciate your character strengths. You can find positive events in your daily life. You can imagine your ideal self in five years and consider several realistic pathways to reach your ideal self.

lessons.content: ・Orientation (course objectives, how the course is conducted, schedule, and assessment methods). ・Learn about the concept of wellbeing. ・Understand your own current state of wellbeing. ・Learn how to take the VIA-IS psychological test.
lessons.operation: Slideshow presentation covering the syllabus for this course. Group activity - Discussion about your own day to day life in using the PERMA model as a guide. Take the PERMA-Profiler KIT version (online). Go over handout covering how to take the VIA-IS test.
lessons.assignments: Take the VIA-IS test, save the results, and bring the results to the next class.

lessons.content: ・Learn the proper attitude and skills required for constructive listening. ・Understand and appreciate own character strengths.
lessons.operation: Workshop - Utilize the VIA-IS results to practice constructive listening using listening skills such as having a proper attitude, using minimal encouragement and restatements, and asking open ended questions.
lessons.assignments: Use your character strengths in new ways. Record the results and submit at the next class.

lessons.content: ・Character strengths and diversity ・Learn how to improve your well-being using the “Three Good Things” (TGT) activity.
lessons.operation: Group activity - Share the results of using your character strengths in new ways with the group, and then share with the class. Collect the “Using your strengths in the new ways” activity report. Lecture and activity - Learn how to do the “Three Good Things” (TGT) activity and do practice activities.
lessons.assignments: Do the TGT activity using the activity report sheet. Submit the report at the next class.

lessons.content: ・Review and elaborate on the TGT activity. ・Learn about the concept of assertion and do experiential activities.
lessons.operation: Group activity - Share results of the TGT activity in small groups and then with the entire class. Lecture and workshop - Lecture about the concept of assertion, do a warm-up activity, make a skit in small groups and share it with the class. Group activity - Think about how to apply appropriate communication strategies to events from the TGT homework.
lessons.assignments: Do the TGT homework involving appropriate communication skills and submit at the next class.

lessons.content: ・Evaluate the positive things you decided on your own. ・Consider what your ideal future self can be like by doing the Best Possible Selves (BPS) activity.
lessons.operation: Group Activity - Share the results of the communication-based TGT activity in groups and then with the entire class. Q&A - Address any issues that come up regarding the TGT activity and recording. Then, collect the record sheets. Lecture and workshop - Learn how to do the BPS activity. Then in pairs, work together to complete the BPS activity. Finally, share your partner's BPS with the small group. Explain the homework, which will be the actual BPS activity.
lessons.assignments: Do the BPS activity and submit at the next class.

lessons.content: ・Understand and appreciate diversity through the BPS activity. ・Consider a realistic best possible future self. ・Think of realistic pathways to reach your goals.
lessons.operation: Group activity - Share the results of the BPS activity with the group to learn that there are many different kinds of best possible future selves. Collect record sheet after activity. Workshop - Think of a realistic version of your best possible future self in 5 years. Think about pathways to reach this version of your best possible self. Lecture - Consider the gap between plans and reality and learn ways to do address adversity that will come your way in the future.
lessons.assignments: Write a report of your best possible future (5 years from now) self. Include a specific situation, the pathways you took to get there, and the steps you took to address the adversity encountered along the way. Submit at the next class.

lessons.content: ・Review the things learned throughout this course, including reflecting on your own psychological growth. ・Know and appreciate your own change in well-being.
lessons.operation: Take the PERMA-Profiler KIT version (online) and compare the results to those from the first class. Presentation - 2 minutes per person, reflect and share your thoughts about the course using the educational objectives as a guide. Submit presentation report. Instructor evaluation. Course evaluation.
